# System Security Plan — input document

This is the SSP input for **Shipyard AI Onboard + WADL** (Work Authorization
Decision Layer), written to be lifted into an authorization package. Every
implementation statement names its enforcement and its verification — a CI
job, a generated test, or a check in `scripts/self-assessment.sh` (IDs
`WADL-SA-nn`) — because a control statement nothing verifies is prose, not
posture. Companion documents: `docs/production-posture.md` (the standing
policy and NIST anchor map), `docs/poam.md` (known gaps with closure paths),
`deploy/README.md` and `deploy/wadl.service` (the deployment shape).

## 1. System identification

- **Function.** Availability planning and work-authorization *decision
  support* for naval shipyard availabilities: schedule ingest (Primavera P6),
  compartment/zone state, authorization findings, sequence and mitigation
  options. The system renders verdicts and evidence; it does not actuate
  anything and every response self-describes as `decision_support_only`.
- **Architecture.** One Rust binary (API + built web shell) behind the
  yard's accredited TLS/CAC terminator, PostgreSQL when deployed (the
  `postgres` cargo feature; an in-memory store serves the demo), no other
  services, no outbound connections of any kind.
- **Data.** Schedule, work-order, compartment and hazard data per tenant
  organization; no PII beyond operator identifiers asserted by the identity
  proxy; no classified handling claimed — enclave placement is the
  deploying activity's determination.

## 2. Authorization boundary and data flows

Inside the boundary: the `serve` binary and its database. Every ingress is
one TCP listener (loopback by default, `WADL_BIND` to widen behind the
terminator). There is **no egress**: the binary initiates no outbound
connections — no telemetry, no CDN, no font or script origins (the CSP
enforces the same fact browser-side). Data enters by exactly two doors:

1. HTTPS requests via the terminator, carrying proxy-asserted identity.
2. Bulk imports (P6 XER, zone/budget CSV) through the three import
   endpoints, all-or-nothing with dry-run preview and typed refusals.

## 4. Enforcement parameters (read from the code)

| Parameter | Value | Where enforced |
|---|---|---|
| Concurrent requests in flight | {max_in_flight} (then immediate 503) | `wadl_api::hardening` semaphore |
| Request timeout | {timeout_secs} s to first response | `wadl_api::hardening` |
| Import body ceiling | {import_mb} MB, import doors only | `read_import_body`, after scope check |
| Other request bodies | axum default (small) | router default |
| Bind address | `127.0.0.1` unless `WADL_BIND` set | `serve` binary |
| Identity trust | dev shim, or proxy-asserted when `WADL_PROXY_KEY` set | `wadl-api` auth extractor |
| Person | required in proxy mode (`x-wadl-person`); `dev:anonymous` on the shim | `wadl-api` auth extractor; hashed into every ledger row |
| Roles without `x-wadl-roles` | `reader`, or `WADL_DEFAULT_ROLES` when set | `wadl-api` auth extractor; refused at boot if unknown |
| Store | in-memory demo; PostgreSQL when built with the `postgres` feature and `DATABASE_URL` is set (RLS armed per request) | `serve` binary + `wadl-store` |

## 5. Control implementation statements

Status vocabulary: **Implemented** (in this tree, verified), **Hybrid**
(split with the deploying environment; the environment's share is named),
**Planned** (open in `docs/poam.md`).

### AC — Access Control

- **AC-2 / AC-3 / AC-4 (Implemented).** Identity enters at one extractor;
  every scoped handler resolves a `TenantScope` (tenant + per-hull
  assignment) before touching data, and PostgreSQL row-level security
  enforces the same boundary independently — a skipped check and a dropped
  policy each fail CI on their own (`leak-tests`, `migrations` jobs).
  Cross-tenant reads return not-found, never a distinguishable refusal.
  *Verified by:* generated leak tests; `pg_rls` on live PostgreSQL;
  WADL-SA-03/04.
- **AC-6 (Implemented).** Assignment is per hull; `GET /api/whoami` serves
  the caller's resolved scope, trust mode, person, roles and capabilities,
  and the shell wears them in its chrome — the signed-in block shows what
  the server resolved, and a session admitted by the dev shim is marked
  with an amber badge so it can never pass for an authenticated one in a
  screenshot. Least privilege is a code table (`wadl_api::roles::MATRIX`,
  eight roles, six capabilities, served on `whoami` as `role_matrix`) and
  one `route_layer` gate over every write route (`roles::GATED`): a role
  without the capability is refused 403 with a sentence naming who holds
  it, nothing is written, and a dry run is never refused. Proxy users
  arriving without roles are `reader` unless the deployment sets
  `WADL_DEFAULT_ROLES` (an SSP-visible decision, refused at boot if it
  names an unknown role).
  *Verified by:* generated weakest-role tests (one per gated route, as a
  `reader`, 403); `roles` unit tests place every POST; WADL-SA-06/11.
- **AC-11 / AC-12 (Hybrid).** Session locking, idle timeout, and
  re-authentication are the identity terminator/broker's share, with the
  required settings in `deploy/README.md` §Session lifetime. The binary is
  stateless per request, so a terminated session loses everything at once.

### AU — Audit and Accountability

- **AU-2 / AU-3 (Implemented).** One JSON object per request on stdout —
  timestamp, method, path, status, duration, asserted tenant and asserted
  person — for every `/api` request and every non-2xx anywhere; refusals
  (401/403/404/413/422/503) are logged at least as loudly as successes.
  Decisions, clearances, acknowledgements, proposals and every document
  commit or revert are additionally recorded in the domain ledger with the
  person who acted and the rationale.
  *Verified by:* WADL-SA-07 (behavioral); audit layer is outermost in
  `wadl_api::hardening::harden`; `identity` integration tests read the
  person back off the ledger.
- **AU-9 / AU-10 (Hybrid).** The hash-chained ledger is verifiable with
  `wadl-cli verify-ledger` (non-repudiation of recorded decisions). From
  migration 0017 every row is chain format 2: the acting person's id and
  display name are inside the row's hash, so a row cannot be re-attributed
  without breaking the chain; rows from before are format 1 and verify in
  the same chain, honestly unattributed. Transport-log integrity is
  journald's sealing/forwarding under `deploy/wadl.service`.
  *Verified by:* `ledger` unit tests (v1→v2 switch, altered actor breaks);
  `pg_rls` round trip on live PostgreSQL.

### CM — Configuration Management

- **CM-2 / CM-6 (Implemented).** Configuration is environment-only and
  enumerated in the serve binary's doc header; unparseable values fall back
  to safe defaults (loopback, 8080). There is no config file to drift.
- **CM-7 (Implemented).** Least functionality by construction: database
  driver compiled in only under the `postgres` feature, workspace
  dependencies declare `default-features = false`, no CORS layer exists,
  and the systemd unit drops all capabilities and filters syscalls.
  *Verified by:* featureless `cargo test --workspace` in CI proves the
  no-sqlx tree; WADL-SA-01/02.

### IA — Identification and Authentication

- **IA-2 / IA-8 (Hybrid).** CAC/PIV (or the enclave's broker) authenticates
  at the accredited terminator; the binary trusts identity assertions only
  from that hop, proven by the `WADL_PROXY_KEY` shared key compared in
  constant time. Requests reaching the port without it are refused before
  identity is read. On that hop the terminator asserts the person
  (`x-wadl-person`, the certificate's stable subject — required, 401
  without it), a percent-encoded display name (`x-wadl-person-name`,
  display only, falls back to the id) and role codes (`x-wadl-roles`);
  the six-header contract is `docs/briefs/proxy-owner-contract.md`. The
  terminator must strip all six from client traffic (`deploy/README.md`).
  *Verified by:* auth unit tests (both modes, person, name, roles);
  WADL-SA-05/06/11.

### RA / SA — Risk Assessment, Acquisition

- **RA-5 / SA-11 (Implemented).** Every push: `cargo deny` (advisories,
  licenses, bans, sources), clippy as errors with `unsafe` forbidden and
  panics denied in serving code, full test suites, SPDX SBOM emitted as a
  build artifact from both lockfiles. Air-gapped builds are rehearsed in CI
  (`cargo vendor` + `--offline`); release reproducibility is checked on
  demand (two clean builds, matching hashes).
- **SA-22 (Implemented).** Dependency admission policy in
  `docs/production-posture.md` Pillar 1; the tracing stack was removed
  under it.

### SC — System and Communications Protection

- **SC-5 (Implemented).** Overload sheds loudly (semaphore → immediate
  503), requests time out, import bodies are capped at the named doors only
  and read after the scope check. *Verified by:* body-cap tests in
  `wadl-api`; WADL-SA-08.
- **SC-8 (Hybrid).** TLS terminates at the yard's accredited terminator;
  the binary binds loopback by default so plaintext never leaves the host
  unless explicitly configured otherwise.
- **SC-39 (Implemented, deployment).** `deploy/wadl.service`: DynamicUser,
  `ProtectSystem=strict`, empty capability set, `@system-service` seccomp
  allow-list, `MemoryDenyWriteExecute`, loopback-only address families.

### SI — System and Information Integrity

- **SI-10 (Implemented).** Imports are all-or-nothing with dry-run preview
  and typed refusals (a file with no activities is refused, not partially
  loaded); XER parsing carries structural caps; `as_of` instants outside
  the availability are refused, not clamped. *Verified by:* import-door
  test suite.
- **SI-11 (Implemented).** Errors leave as `application/problem+json` with
  no SQL text, stack detail, or foreign identifiers; backend detail goes to
  stderr diagnostics only. *Verified by:* WADL-SA-09/10.
